Sudan Tribune’s August 12 report attributes completed processing and actual departures/arrivals to the Gedaref police chief; it is not direct journalist observation. phases.Qualification:
Passenger denial is reported for February 28, 2019 and directly observed on March 1; exact first onset remains unresolved. Dated denials and selective permissions do not establish a continuous 2019–2022 all-traffic closure. Preserve February 28 freight diversion, June 10–22 truck trial, January 31, 2022 cargo/returnee permission, March 7 outgoing bus and later local-shopping relaxation as different scopes. Freight eligibility remains contested; national COVID policy is GL04.

GL01-R1: Formal heavy-truck diversion effective February 28 until June 10 trial permission. RRA officially cited construction; Ugandan officials disputed this and alleged broader passenger denials. Eligibility of a construction-only diversion is not independently established; record remains eligible for documented coercive movement restrictions. Alternative routes remained available; no actual first-trial passage time established.

GL01-R2: Observed June 23 around 01:00 reclosure; January 31 2022 cargo resumption only. URN quotes an unnamed officer citing structural cracks, while reporting broader political allegations and travel restrictions. Political character is contested for the narrowly scoped freight measure; continuity relies on retrospective reporting and overlaps pandemic rules.

GL01-C7RWP1: The EastAfrican March 1 report describes the previous Thursday, February 28, when a Gatuna bus was allowed through after its Rwandan passengers and driver were refused; it also directly observes nationality-selective access on March 1. Neither is necessarily the first onset. Ugandan official accounts indicate earlier restrictions; Kigali officials described an advisory and denied a general closure. Construction claims do not erase the separate passenger evidence.

GL01-C7RWP2: Further dated confirmation, not proof of uninterrupted enforcement since March. August ministerial statement supports continuing advisory language, not universal denial.

GL01-C7RWP3: Last-confirmed is report date, not first relaxation. Roughly two-month retrospective description is not converted to an exact onset. Detailed anonymous interview concerns Kagitumba; introduction names Gatuna. One outlet does not establish uniform gate practice.

GL01-C7RWP4: Date-specific observation; no continuity from 2019 inferred. Cargo, Rwandan citizens and returning residents could enter Rwanda. National COVID policy is GL04; exact political/health overlap unresolved.

GL01-C7RWP5: No reverse passenger vehicle observed by the report’s 17:00 cutoff. Some passengers could not meet testing costs. National permission and this passage do not establish all-gate/group normalization; Cyanika ID travel remained restricted. Onset and continuous duration unknown.

GL01-C7RWP6: Calendar normalization of a dated relative reference, not a retrieved order. Local shopping differs from earlier passenger permission; food limits and changed testing remain. Do not extrapolate to every gate, traveler or commodity; onset and duration unknown.
